A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EKAN work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections and appendices.

before.justification: V2 reports original EKAN experiments on particle scattering, three-body prediction, and top-quark tagging, with test MSE and accuracy results in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds reported comparisons involving augmented baselines and CGENN in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The gated spline basis functions, equivariant linear weights, lift layer, stacked architecture, and grid-update procedure are unchanged. Moving the grid-update description to Appendix D does not introduce a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use particle-scattering regression, planar three-body prediction from four preceding time steps, and top-quark classification using three jet constituents. The added comparator configurations retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add MLP + augmentation and KAN + augmentation to each task's comparison set. Table 3 additionally evaluates CGENN alongside EMLP. This substantially broadens the comparisons while retaining every previously evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V3 adds augmentation conditions for MLP/KAN and specifies CGENN with O(1,3) equivariance, four layers, and hidden width 200 for top-quark tagging. Existing splits, metrics, model settings, and training budgets remain unchanged. The augmentation procedure is unspecified.

E4.justification: Tables 1–3 newly compare MLP/KAN with and without augmentation, examining augmentation's contribution to performance. V3 removes the inference-time versus parameter-count analysis in v2 Table 5. No EKAN component ablation or distribution-shift test is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs with different random seeds for the three tasks. The added result rows follow this existing practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test appears.

E6.justification: All shared benchmark means and standard deviations are unchanged, but v3 adds augmentation results across all tasks and CGENN tagging results. At 10^4 training samples, CGENN reports 77.05 ± 0.03% accuracy with 85K parameters, alongside EKAN's retained 76.93% with 34K. V2's scattering and tagging timings and its 7–16 ms three-body timing series are removed.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 becomes Theorem 4.1 with the same equivariance statement and proof. Group definitions, generators, and mathematical constructions are retained. The EMLP constraint derivation and grid-update algebra move to Appendices B and D without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and third contribution replace matching EMLP with 26% of its parameters with matching state-of-the-art equivariant architectures using fewer than 40%, reflecting the added CGENN comparison. The main novelty, general-framework, and data-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 Section 6.3 explicitly excludes task-specific jet-tagging methods from the primary benchmark and proposes combining them with EKAN as future work; v3 removes this qualification and proposal. The explanation connecting unobserved constituents to non-symbolic prediction remains.

D1.justification: V3 documents CGENN's group and model configuration and adds a direct DOI link to the existing top-quark dataset reference. It removes all EKAN inference-time disclosures while retaining the optimizer, learning rates, training schedules, hardware, and model-width table.

R1.justification: V3 adds Ruhe et al. (2023) for CGENN and removes Bogatskiy et al. (2020), Gong et al. (2022), and Qu and Gouskos (2020), together with the specialized jet-tagging discussion. The broader KAN and equivariance positioning remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: V3 shortens the EMLP motivation, converts the contribution bullets into a paragraph, moves EMLP background and grid updates to appendices, and adds a generic Impact Statement. Most scientific prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1–4 expand from tightly compressed single-column displays to full-width tables; Tables 1–3 gain comparator rows, and Table 5 disappears. Figure 1 drops the MLP/EMLP panels and moves earlier. The document also adopts different title/header formatting and single-column appendices, substantially changing presentation and table legibility.

improvement.justification: The augmented-baseline comparisons and CGENN evaluation strengthen the comparative evidence, while the enlarged tables make results substantially easier to inspect. These gains provide a limited net improvement, tempered by unspecified augmentation procedures, removal of inference-time evidence, and loss of the explicit qualification about specialized jet-tagging benchmarks.
